sources.kmd: bc250-win 1aade92b (train/b26), the b26 train driver 0.7.216.25, escape ABI 0x000700D8 (unchanged since 0.7.216.1). Three kernel changes ride this train. The idle telemetry cadence (BD-097, the long-idle row): at the governor's own idle state the periodic telemetry block comes every 120 s instead of 60 s, so the 768-line ring holds over an hour of idle desktop; under load the period stays 5 s, and every state change still writes its own line where it happens. The VM flush on the gfx ring (option (b) of docs/design/gfx-submit-root-serialization.md): with EnableRingVmFlush 1 the page-table root write and the invalidation request/acknowledge wait are 29 PM4 dwords in front of the job frame, instead of the MMIO write pair and the CPU poll; the release default is absent, and with the value absent or 0 the frame is the 23 dwords of 0.7.216.24, dword for dword, which a host gate holds against a frozen array. The DP audio container ID (step 4 of docs/design/dp-audio.md): DxgkDdiGetChildContainerId answers STATUS_MONITOR_NO_DESCRIPTOR and keeps the container ID the operating system offers, and the port ID of that call goes into the endpoint's ELD (SINK_INFO2 and SINK_INFO3) with one presence cycle and a read-back, behind EnableDpAudioContainerId, 1 by default. The escape record of the audio sequence is ABI 3, 536 bytes, with the ABI 1 and ABI 2 prefixes frozen. Built with /Brepro and a sorted object list. Two builds, each into an empty directory (scratch/train/b26-build/kmd/a and kmd/b), gave the same unsigned and signed image; only the catalog differs between them, because each build signs a new one Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.23: bc250-win 00f09bfa (train/b25), the b25 train driver 0.7.216.24, escape ABI 0x000700D8 (unchanged since 0.7.216.1). Three kernel changes ride this train. BD-097: the GuardLog line of each SDMA paging submit is rate-limited by driver/kmd/log_rate.h (the first lines, then one summary with a count per interval), and the log summary escape writes its block into a side buffer instead of the ring, so the overlay's summary poll no longer rotates the whole ring in twelve seconds. BD-094: the CPU restore baseline is a measured boost ceiling (CpuBoostProbe, a 25 ms busy window), a clock limit is refused while the ceiling is unknown, and a refused clock limit does not cost the stored undervolt. BD-104: DriverVersionStart writes the adapter's software key first, by the handle of IoOpenDeviceRegistryKey with PLUGPLAY_REGKEY_DRIVER, and visits the numbered video keys after it, because those keys do not exist yet inside DxgkDdiStartDevice and each of them is a REG_LINK to that same software key. Built with /Brepro and a sorted object list. Two builds, each into an empty directory (scratch/train/b25-build/kmd/a and kmd/c), gave the same unsigned and signed image; only the catalog differs between them, because each build signs a new one. The revision moved from 0.7.216.23 to 0.7.216.24 at the cut: both kernel wagons were written while 0.7.216.23 was free and train b24 shipped that number Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.22: bc250-win 1884b33d (train/b24), the b24 train driver 0.7.216.23, escape ABI 0x000700D8 (unchanged since 0.7.216.1). Two builds, each into an empty directory (scratch/train/b24-build/kmd/a at 417788e4 and scratch/train/b24-build/kmd/b at the head), gave the same unsigned image (A0CDEC73) and the same signed bc250kmd.sys (27A9AE29); only the catalog differs between them, because each build signs a new one. Everything below is the tester.23 text for these bytes. mesa fork amdgpu-wddm/b25-system-icd d3da6d0a: amdgpu-wddm/b25-system aa1bd395 over the shipped tester.22 line amdgpu-wddm/bd102-system 31d3f390, with the system half of the dispatch-table generator fix merged onto it (amdgpu-wddm/b25-gen-x86 eca7adc9). The Windows shader disk cache, so a native Vulkan game does not recompile every pipeline at each start (GitHub #10, 11 commits, the upstream Windows guard dropped). -Db_ndebug=true in the radv-system option set, so no RADV assert is live: a failed assert calls abort() in the game process and the game ends with no message, and every release up to tester.22 shipped this ICD with the asserts on. The BD-102 review's fence-wait shape: GetDeviceState runs only after a wait that failed or timed out or a fence that did not advance, not on every blocking wait whose quick poll missed. The generator merge puts APIENTRY on the 40 not-supported dispatch stubs and one #ifndef per STATUS_* name; on x64 that changes no code generation, and it is what makes an x86 build of this line exist at all. This is the ICD that carries the owner's Quake II RTX release gate, and every one of those changes is in code Quake II RTX runs, so the b24 proof does not carry over: the gate is re-run on these bytes Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.22: mesa fork amdgpu-wddm/bd102-system 31d3f390, the BD-102 fix line over the b23 round-4 system head 468ca20d. BD-094 (GitHub #26): the restore baseline is the boost ceiling that CpuBoostProbe measures in a 25 ms busy window, not the per-core clock of the moment, so a revert, a reset or the end of the joint arm's cap gives back the firmware boost instead of the 3200 MHz an idle processor shows; while the ceiling is unknown a clock limit is refused, and a refused clock limit leaves the stored undervolt alone. BD-104: the AMD-scheme DriverVersion goes to the adapter's own software key, opened with IoOpenDeviceRegistryKey and PLUGPLAY_REGKEY_DRIVER, which is the key DXGK_DEVICE_INFO.DeviceRegistryPath names and the key a graphics miniport is told to write; the numbered Control\Video keys are visited after it and are no longer the only way in, because inside DxgkDdiStartDevice they do not exist yet. That is what the b24 lab session measured: the start logged 'this adapter has no video key' about a key the same script read minutes later, so C69 shipped inert in tester.22 and this driver makes the setting do what it exists for. Built with /Brepro and a sorted object list, 897 functions with unwind data, largest fixed frame 3992 bytes. New in b24, C69: the AMD-scheme DriverVersion goes to every four-digit subkey of Control\Video\{VideoID}, with the VideoID read from the adapter's hardware key, instead of the software class key that DeviceInfo.DeviceRegistryPath hands out. Each numbered key is a REG_LINK to the class key, so the write lands there and also moves DEVPKEY_Device_DriverVersion, which Unreal Engine 5.4 reads, and the guard line names the key the open reached. ReportAmdDriverVersion 1 of HKLM\SOFTWARE\amdgpu-wddm\Graphics switches it on, 0 puts the installed number back; the b23 lab run 489 showed the old write never reaching the key the engine reads. Built with /Brepro and a sorted object list. Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.21: KMD 0.7.216.22, escape ABI 0x000700D8, unchanged from 0.7.216.1 (bc250-win 0d6b3299, train/b23: the tester.20 driver 0.7.216.14 with the b23 kernel wagons). New in b23, each one a Parameters value away from the behaviour before it. M15.12 stage-1 hang recovery (HangRecoveryMode, absent = 1): a node-0 engine reset kills the hung job's VMID waves through the GFX register path and, when the ring drains, reports the reset as done, so only the process of the hung job loses its device; the verdicts go to Parameters\HangRecovery. Display modes stage A (EnableDisplayModes 2): the EDID over DP AUX, the monitor descriptor, the native mode and smaller sizes scaled by the DCN scaler at the native timing, and the DP audio endpoint takes its sink from the EDID (step 4). Per-flip plane pixel formats RGBA8 and RGB10A2 for independent flip, with the firmware's B8G8R8A8 written back at stop, bugcheck and the desktop's next flip (EnableScanoutPlaneFormats 1), and the scan-out caps trailer carries the committed source mode. The telemetry block runs every 60 s at the DPM idle point, so the 1024-line ring keeps its events (BD-097). Start health CONFIRMED follows the confirmed start generation through mode and visibility changes (BD-098). ReportAmdDriverVersion 1 of HKLM\SOFTWARE\amdgpu-wddm\Graphics makes the start write an AMD-scheme DriverVersion into the adapter's software key and puts the installed number back when the setting is cleared (C69). The CPU restore baseline is the highest clock the firmware answered over the P-state table and the per-core clocks, clamped to 3500 MHz, so a revert, a reset or the end of the joint arm's cap gives back the firmware boost, not the 3200 MHz table top (BD-094, K137, 424b2945). The kernel is built with /Brepro and a sorted object list. The b22 changes: New in b22, each one a Parameters value away from the behaviour before it. A runtime restart of the GPU device inside a confirmed boot works: an orderly stop gives the boot-loop guard its start back, a second teardown of the same device is refused by a StopDone guard instead of running twice, the release of the display fills the scanned-out surface with black, and CreateDevice logs the process it answered (BD-090). The DisplayPort audio path reads the Azalia, DIO and DCCG state for the check table and clears DIO_MEM_PWR_CTRL before it enables the stream, as Linux dcn201_init_hw does. The clock governor holds its idle point while the work on the GPU still fits that point (DpmIdleLeavePermille 150), which stops the 500 and 1000 MHz flapping of an idle desktop, and it carries the C62 joint power arm that caps the processor for a bound and hot GPU, behind DpmJointGovernor, which is 0 in this release. Memory manager stage 1: the OS aperture is 384 MiB (ApertureSegmentMegabytes, absent = 384, clamped to 256..447, one fallback to 256 if the GART refuses), a VRAM allocation of the user-mode driver that is neither a scan-out surface nor DISCARDABLE is also resident in the aperture segment so Windows can move it to system memory instead of evicting it (EnableSharedResidency, absent = 1), and the vidmm and paging counters now report what moved. The SMU owner is refused with a log line instead of a failed start when BAR5 is not mapped, and the log ring is kept in one file per device start and per stop under C:/BC250/kmdlog, with 200-file pruning (BD-091). The kernel is built with /Brepro and a sorted object list, and two builds of this head into empty directories gave the same unsigned and signed bytes. The b21 changes against 0.7.213.1 are all here too, each on by every install with one Parameters value that takes it away again. A VMID per page-table root from a pool of up to 14, so a job of another process does not wait for the ring to drain (EnableVmidPool, 0.7.214). The case fan control: the driver takes fan 1 from the BIOS curve while it runs, drives it on its own curve (Standard: 100 % from 80 C) and gives it back to the chip on every exit path, through escape 30 RUN_FAN (EnableFanControl); a leased mode ends with the durable mode from before it. DisplayPort audio steps 0 to 2: the Azalia endpoint of the running DP stream is configured, the audio stream of that DP encoder is started (audio DTO1, AFMT, DP SEC), and only then is the endpoint present to the inbox HD Audio driver, through escape 31 RUN_DPAUDIO ABI 2 (EnableDpAudio, EnableDpAudioEndpoint, EnableDpAudioStream; 0.7.215.1 showed the endpoint with no audio clock, so no sound and video at about 0.7x). The SMU metrics table once a second for the package power, RUN_DPM ABI 3; a 0 mW table is a skipped sample (EnableSmuMetrics). The CPU tuning surface is open by default (CpuTune 1): a change runs only on an administrator's request, as a trial that reverts by itself. Re-signed with the release certificate, code unchanged
